extracted.intended_audience: General readers and fans of Saturday Night Live / sketch comedy
extracted.subtask_description: A short listicle describing nine SNL sketches that were cut at dress rehearsal and briefly summarizing why each sketch didn't make the live show (e.g., performer breakdowns, producer decisions, rehearsal mishaps).

rubrics_metrics.name: Cast breaks/laughing prevents clear delivery
rubrics_metrics.description: This sketch probably got cut because Bill Hader and Fred Armisen spent the entire thing laughing so hard that they couldn’t speak clearly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When performers repeatedly break character or cannot speak their lines clearly due to laughing, the sketch often fails in dress rehearsal and is removed from the live show.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unexplained producer decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: This sketch become a cult favorite after it was included on a Best of Will Ferrell DVD. It’s pretty great and, as far as I know, there has never been any public explanation offered about why it was cut. Lorne Michaels moves in mysterious ways.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Producers may cut sketches for reasons that are not publicly explained; a sketch's later popularity or quality doesn't guarantee it will air.

rubrics_metrics.name: Producers reject a concept
rubrics_metrics.description: Wanna see the pop star as a salty dog boat captain? Well, the Producers apparently didn't.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even appealing concepts or celebrity ideas can be rejected by producers during pre-broadcast selection.

rubrics_metrics.name: Performer unable to deliver lines
rubrics_metrics.description: In this cut segment from Weekend Update, the late, great Chris Farley just can’t quite spit out what he’s trying to say.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a performer cannot clearly deliver the joke or articulate the bit during rehearsal, the segment is unlikely to air.

rubrics_metrics.name: High-profile guest sketches can still be cut
rubrics_metrics.description: Who in their right mind would cut a sketch of Shaq cradling Will Ferrell in his arms as they sing a song together?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Star power or visually amusing pairings do not guarantee inclusion; timing, pacing, or fit with the show can lead to cuts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dress rehearsal disasters / unscripted breakdowns
rubrics_metrics.description: Justin Bieber Almost Dies — As an added bonus to this clip, Bill Hader and two SNL writers offer some context on this sketch that went horribly wrong in dress rehearsal. You’ll pretty much see right away why this was cut. The sketch features the unscripted line 'The stage almost fell on you,' and then devolves from there.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Technical mishaps, safety issues, or unscripted lines that derail the performance at dress rehearsal commonly cause sketches to be cut.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tone/content of concept may prompt cut
rubrics_metrics.description: The Elf on the Shelf — Bobby Moynihan portrays the newly-required Christmas tradition as a serious Narc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Satirical takes or tonal choices (e.g., portraying a novelty as a serious personality) may be judged unsuitable for the show; no specific reason for the cut is provided here.

rubrics_metrics.name: Host/guest concept sketches may not fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Timberlake as Mozart — This sketches shows perennial host Justin Timberlake taking on the role of the great composer planning a break from music to become an actor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concept sketches featuring hosts in historical or oddball roles may be dropped if they don't land or fit the episode; the article gives no explicit reason for this cut.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ideas that can't get past rehearsal
rubrics_metrics.description: Andy Samberg’s Bathroom Habit — In this clip from Conan, the former cast member explains one sketch idea he had that he could never get past the dress rehearsal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some sketch ideas repeatedly fail during rehearsals (timing, delivery, or concept issues) and therefore never make it to the live broadcast.
